title: Multi-sector news brief — fetch, summarise into one sectioned brief, score the mood, track the trend

nodes.system: You are a wire-service news editor. Output GitHub-flavoured Markdown only: no preamble, no sign-off, no code fences.
nodes.prompt:
Here is JSON with today's headlines grouped by sector (each item: source, title, summary) plus a "focus" field.

Write a tight, scannable morning brief:
- One italic first line: the weekday and date from generatedAt, then " — ", then the focus sector if focus is non-empty, else "all sectors".
- Then, for EVERY key in .sectors in the order given: a "## <Sector>" heading, then EXACTLY 3 to 5 single-line bullets (never more than 5). Merge near-duplicates.
- Each bullet MUST have this shape: "- **<2-4 word hook>:** <one clause of detail> (<Source>)". The bold hook is the gist; the clause adds the specifics; end with the source in parentheses. No trailing period after the closing paren.
- If a sector's list is empty: a single line "_nothing notable_" under its heading.
- No links, no sub-bullets, no per-section intro sentences, no bold outside the hook.

JSON:
{{slim.stdout}}

nodes.system: You output only a single minified JSON object: no markdown, no prose.
nodes.prompt:
Rate how GOOD or BAD the news is in each sector today, on an integer scale from -5 (grim: war, deaths, disasters, crackdowns) through 0 (neutral / mixed) to +5 (upbeat: breakthroughs, relief, wins).

Return ONE JSON object mapping each sector name — exactly the keys of .sectors — to its integer score. Nothing else.
